journey:sallman-head-of-christ.noimg: © Warner Press. The original painting is in the Warner Sallman collection at Anderson University, Indiana.

x.summary: Sallman's soft-focus profile of Christ, gazing upward in warm light, may be the most widely reproduced image of Jesus ever made. For much of the twentieth century it hung in churches, Sunday schools and homes, and was printed on calendars, Bibles and wallet cards across North America and beyond. Its gentle, approachable Christ shaped how millions of people imagined Jesus, and its image of a fair-featured Christ has also prompted much discussion about race and representation.
facts: The 1940 painting grew out of a charcoal sketch, 'The Son of Man,' that Sallman drew in 1924 for the cover of the Covenant Companion, the magazine of the Evangelical Covenant Church.
During the Second World War, the Salvation Army and the YMCA, as members of the USO, handed out pocket-sized copies to American servicemen heading overseas.
By the end of the twentieth century it had been reproduced more than 500 million times.
